body:
CANONICAL: Greg's throughput decisions for Engram (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-06; split from rules-greg-direction for size). These are Greg's words, relayed by Engram::Advisor in mailbox-74a6af16; they carry no higher authority than his current word and grant no new commit, push or install act.

#1030, 2026-10-06 00:27Z, verbatim: "Start Architect2 as the third Engram implementer on w-0c66e05fb5d0 + w-9696aa09b59a, using a non-store-format bounded/count-by-root design; do not propose or make a durable schema change. Run the standing design review during current gates. Keep gates and landings serial. Batching/fast-forward policy changes are not authorized by this message; I will return with Greg's decision."

#1031, 2026-10-06 00:29Z, verbatim: "Greg adopts the council recommendation on throughput: use a fast-forward landing for a small item only when it was frozen and validated on the exact current master and master has not moved; retain the full gate/review/evaluation evidence. Do not create larger batches merely to save gates right now. Apply this to Engram's eligible small items and record the process decision."

PROCESS DECISION, as Engram::Fable applies it:
- Three implementers: Engram::Coder, Engram::Opus, Engram::Architect2. One full gate at a time, granted by LAUNCH NOW; one landing window at a time.
- A small item lands by fast-forward only when its freeze, full gate, review pair and fresh evaluation were all on the exact current master, and master has not moved since the freeze. Nothing is skipped: the full gate, pair and evaluation evidence stay required.
- When master moved, the round is carried onto the new master, re-frozen and redone (the exact-tree rule, unchanged).
- Items are not bundled merely to save gates. A bundle needs its own reason, such as one shared file, one defect or one acceptance criterion. This retracts the P3 bundle (w-228b9d786330, w-86dff02b8674, w-8be5bcaa1588) proposed in Engram::Fable's #1029; they go one at a time unless such a reason applies.
- To keep the fast-forward case common, the coordinator grants LAUNCH NOW to the round whose base is current master, and the next implementer freezes only after "master is X".

CONTINUOUS PIPELINE AND CODER MODEL (Greg, relayed by Engram::Advisor, mailbox-74a6af16).
#1314 (2026-10-13 02:36Z): "Greg directs a continuous implementation pipeline now. Prefer Codex gpt-6.1-sol for coding agents. Immediately provision or reassign available Codex Sol coders to prepared, in-scope Engram tasks; keep each coder with one claim and worktree, and have the next implementation prepared while a serial gate runs. Do not wait idly for a gate unless a real dependency requires it. Preserve serial gate and landing windows."
#1319 (02:44Z), verbatim: "Greg confirms Codex gpt-6.1-sol is the preferred implementation model. Apply it by default to every new coder assignment. Use a different model only when Sol is unavailable or moving already-started work would cost more than continuing it; record that exception. Do not interrupt Merger's current w-b411 design review merely to swap its model."
How Engram::Fable applies it:
- Every new coder assignment goes to a Codex gpt-6.1-sol session. An exception is recorded on the item.
- Agents cannot create ROOT sessions (TermAl w-98d0add8c5bb). Fresh Sol roots come from Greg in the TermAl UI, via the Advisor; otherwise idle existing Sol roots are reassigned.
- While an item waits for or runs its gate, its coder does only read-only preparation of its next item (design, explorer review). It claims that item after landing.
- Builds stay serialized around gates: no WSL during any gate, and at most one granted filtered test during the other project's gate.
